record.paper_title: Gradings, Braidings, Representations, Paraparticles: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: Can the braided tensor-product construction for P_B and P_F be generalized to the mixed paraparticle algebras P_BF and P_FB, where P_BF is the Relative Parabose Set and P_FB is the Relative Parafermi Set mixing parabosonic and parafermionic degrees of freedom? This asks whether Fock-like representations of P_BF and P_FB can be extracted as irreducible submodules from graded tensor-product representations of suitable symmetric and antisymmetric Clifford-Weyl quotient algebras, and whether one can develop a multinomial theorem mixing commuting and anticommuting variables.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P_B$ denote the parabosonic algebra (with parabosonic generators satisfying the standard trilinear Green relations) and $P_F$ the parafermionic algebra. Let $P_{BF}$ (the Relative Parabose Set) and $P_{FB}$ (the Relative Parafermi Set) be the mixed paraparticle algebras generated by combining parabosonic and parafermionic degrees of freedom under the two inequivalent choices of relative trilinear (anti)commutation relations between the parabosonic and parafermionic generators (Greenberg–Messiah).

It is known that Fock-like representations of $P_B$ and $P_F$ can be realized by extracting irreducible submodules from braided tensor-product representations of suitable quotients of Clifford–Weyl algebras (the symmetric, respectively antisymmetric, "$W_s$" and "$W_{as}$" quotient algebras, i.e. CCR/CAR-type algebras) on which appropriate braidings act.

(a) Construct an analogous graded/braided tensor-product representation of suitable symmetric and antisymmetric Clifford–Weyl quotient algebras whose decomposition produces, as irreducible submodules, the Fock-like representations of $P_{BF}$ and $P_{FB}$. In particular, identify explicitly the braiding (or grading) used and prove that the resulting irreducible submodules realize the standard Fock representations of $P_{BF}$ and $P_{FB}$.

(b) Develop a multinomial theorem in the resulting algebra that mixes commuting and anticommuting variables, providing closed combinatorial expansion formulas for powers $(x_1 + \cdots + x_n)^N$ when some of the $x_i$ pairwise commute and the remaining $x_j$ pairwise anticommute (with appropriate cross relations matching the chosen braiding).
artifact.category_tag: paraparticle algebras and braided Fock representations
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of extending the braided tensor-product construction of Fock-like representations from the parabose/parafermi algebras to the mixed Relative Parabose/Parafermi sets $P_{BF}$, $P_{FB}$, together with a mixed commuting/anticommuting multinomial theorem, is posed as an open question in the framework of Kanakoglou's paraparticle program. Recent literature (e.g. work on graded paraparticle algebras of Majorana fields, 2024–2025) builds on this framework but does not appear to provide a complete construction and proof for $P_{BF}$ and $P_{FB}$ in the form requested. No resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Gradings, Braidings, Representations, Paraparticles: Some Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: The next step consists of generalizing calculations for the case of the mixed paraparticle algebras PBF and PFB. The philosophy of the method is based on extracting the Fock-like representations of PBF and PFB as irreducible submodules arising in the decomposition of the graded tensor product representations.
status_evidence.claim: The construction for P_BF and P_FB is stated as a program/open problem rather than as a completed result.

status_evidence.title: Super-Hopf realizations of Lie Superalgebras: Braided Paraparticle extensions of the Jordan-Schwinger map
status_evidence.snippet: The mathematical structure of a mixed paraparticle system (Relative Parabose Set) is investigated and a braided group structure is described for it.
status_evidence.claim: Related braided/super-Hopf structure exists but the full Fock-representation extraction and mixed multinomial theorem are not established.
